question.prompt: Four coins are picked out of a piggy bank that contains a collection of pennies, nickels, dimes, and quarters. Which of the following could not be the total value of the four coins, in cents?

solutions.explanation:
The coin values are \(1,5,10,25\) cents, and every listed total is a multiple of \(5\). All coins except pennies contribute multiples of \(5\), so the pennies would also have to contribute a multiple of \(5\). With only four coins, the penny contribution is between \(0\) and \(4\) cents. It must therefore be \(0\).

Without pennies, each coin is worth at least \(5\) cents. Four coins then total at least \(4\cdot5=20\) cents, ruling out \(15\) cents.

Each remaining choice can be made with exactly four allowed coins:
\[
\begin{aligned}
25&=5+5+5+10,\\
35&=5+10+10+10,\\
45&=25+10+5+5,\\
55&=25+10+10+10.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the only impossible listed total is \(\boxed{15}\) cents, choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Use multiples of five
